Gauth, measured

Every value on this page is a CSS variable generated from tokens.json, which was read from www.gauth.com on 2026-10-04: Gauth's own variables where one matches what the page paints, and computed styles of the real elements everywhere else. Each token's source is in the tables. Gauth paints one theme, so this page has no dark mode.

Fonts: Playfair Display, Libre Baskerville, Inter and Shantell Sans load from Google Fonts. Gauth's "SF Pro" is Apple's system face (local only), and the science canvas's "Canvas Print" is Satoshi, which is not on Google Fonts; both fall back to the system UI font here. Covers and illustrations are drawn as tinted placeholders; the real ones are in the screenshots and crops.

Palette

Gauth has no single colour ramp. Its own named colours are the lesson palette (--lesson-*), which the Academy pages paint as well; the rest are literal values its CSS modules paint, grouped here by where they belong.

Roles

The light set: what each colour is used for, as aliases into the palette, plus gradients and component colours.

TokenValueSource

Typography

Two serifs carry the display lines: Libre Baskerville on Homework and Atlas, Playfair Display on Academy and in lessons. Everything else is the system stack, SF Pro, Inter on math cards and dialogs, and Satoshi on the science canvas. The size scale is Gauth's --lesson-font-size-*.

Families

TokenStackSource

Space and shape

Spacing

Radius

Gauth uses many radii: 10 and 12 for controls, 16 for cards, 20 to 28 for dialogs and panels, 32 to 48 for marketing panels, and pills.

Sizes and layout

TokenValueSource

Elevation

Soft, low-alpha shadows. Cards sit on a 4% shadow and deepen to 8% on hover; dialogs and floating panels go up to 16 to 18%. Atlas's prompt box glows peach instead of grey.

Motion

Short and quiet: 160ms for card shadows and fills, Astryx's 125ms with a fast-out curve in the science lesson, a 0.98 press scale on primary buttons, and one spring (the Video Settings popover). Click a track to play its curve.

Focus

Most of Gauth's own controls draw no focus ring at all: the sidebar links, Academy tabs, cards, Create Course, Show more, Start and the unit rail look the same focused as at rest, and the Upgrade and Sign in buttons cannot take focus. Rings exist in three places, each its own colour.

Astryx (science lesson): 2px --action-focus, offset 3px
NewsInsights tabs: 2px #f0023a, offset 2px
SearchAtlas toggle: 2px #171410 at 18%, offset 2px
Narration
Settings row: 2px #307aff, inset 2px

Layout

Read at 1440 x 900. The app shell is a fixed 220px sidebar and a 60px top bar over a centred column; lessons are full screen with no shell.

Science lesson (canvas)

The Sweet Spot
The Sweet Spot
Does Flying Higher Always Save Fuel?

Picture a long-haul jet in cruise. Thinner air means less drag, so should the pilots keep climbing until the airplane reaches its ceiling?

  • The Sweet Spot
  • The Thin Air Advantage
  • The Engine's Breath
  • Finding the Balance

Settings popover, Narration row hovered
The best cruise altitude is a changing sweet spot, not the ceiling, balancing lower drag with lift, thrust, weight, and climb cost.
  1. 1Thin-air advantage: lower density reduces aerodynamic drag.
  2. 2Lift and drag: restore lift, then evaluate total drag.
Takeaway callout and numbered list
Why is "thinner air means less drag" not enough to choose a cruise altitude?
Because lift, thrust, and climb cost also matter
Because drag always rises with altitude
Because aircraft weight increases as fuel burns
Because engines do not use airflow
